title: Using PREVENT Risk Score Functions
text: CVrisk package now includes support American Heart Association’s PREVENT (Predicting Risk cardiovascular disease EVENTs) equations, published 2024. equations provide improved cardiovascular risk prediction compared legacy models like Pooled Cohort Equations (PCE). Implementation Note: PREVENT risk calculations CVrisk powered preventr package, provides comprehensive implementation AHA PREVENT equations. PREVENT equations can predict multiple cardiovascular outcomes (total CVD, ASCVD, heart failure, CHD, stroke), CVrisk focuses specifically ASCVD (atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease) risk maintain consistency legacy risk scores research applications. vignette demonstrates : Use PREVENT functions individually 10-year 30-year risk estimation Leverage different model variants (base, auto, optional predictors) Compare PREVENT scores older ACC/AHA Framingham scores using compute_CVrisk()

title: Using PREVENT Risk Score Functions
text: package provides two main functions: ascvd_10y_prevent() - Calculate 10-year ASCVD risk ascvd_30y_prevent() - Calculate 30-year ASCVD risk functions support multiple model variants model parameter, model = "auto" default, automatically selects best model based available data.

title: Using PREVENT Risk Score Functions
text: PREVENT equations support several model variants preventr package: “auto” (default): Automatically selects best model based available data. recommended setting use cases. “base”: Base model using standard risk factors “hba1c”: Base model + HbA1c (glycated hemoglobin) “uacr”: Base model + UACR (urine albumin--creatinine ratio) “sdi”: Base model + SDI (Social Deprivation Index via ZIP code) “full”: Full model optional predictors

title: Using PREVENT Risk Score Functions
text: model = "auto" (default), preventr package automatically selects appropriate model variant based optional predictors provide data: optional predictors (HbA1c, UACR, ZIP code) provided → uses base model HbA1c provided → uses hba1c model UACR provided → uses uacr model ZIP code provided → uses sdi model multiple optional predictors provided → uses full model incorporating available predictors intelligent selection ensures always get accurate risk estimate based available data, without needing manually specify model variant use. auto-selection examines data patient individually, different patients dataset can use different model variants based available data.

title: Using PREVENT Risk Score Functions
text: base model requires parameters:
code: library(CVrisk)  # Calculate 10-year risk for a 50-year-old female risk_10y <- ascvd_10y_prevent(   gender = "female",   age = 50,   sbp = 160,           # Systolic blood pressure (mm Hg)   bp_med = 1,          # On BP medication (1=Yes, 0=No)   totchol = 200,       # Total cholesterol (mg/dL)   hdl = 45,            # HDL cholesterol (mg/dL)   statin = 0,          # On statin (1=Yes, 0=No)   diabetes = 1,        # Has diabetes (1=Yes, 0=No)   smoker = 0,          # Current smoker (1=Yes, 0=No)   egfr = 90,           # Estimated GFR (mL/min/1.73m²)   bmi = 35             # Body mass index (kg/m²) )  print(risk_10y)  # Returns risk as percentage

title: Using PREVENT Risk Score Functions
text: younger patients, 30-year risk provides better long-term perspective:
code: # Calculate 30-year risk for a 45-year-old male risk_30y <- ascvd_30y_prevent(   gender = "male",   age = 45,   sbp = 130,   bp_med = 0,   totchol = 200,   hdl = 50,   statin = 0,   diabetes = 0,   smoker = 1,          # Current smoker   egfr = 95,   bmi = 28 )  print(risk_30y)

title: Using PREVENT Risk Score Functions
text: HbA1c data available, model automatically uses enhanced equation:
code: # With HbA1c - model will automatically select "hba1c" variant risk_with_hba1c <- ascvd_10y_prevent(   gender = "male",   age = 55,   sbp = 140,   bp_med = 0,   totchol = 213,   hdl = 50,   statin = 0,   diabetes = 1,   smoker = 0,   egfr = 90,   bmi = 30,   hba1c = 7.5,         # Glycated hemoglobin (%)   model = "auto"       # Automatically uses hba1c model )

title: Using PREVENT Risk Score Functions
text: UACR (urine albumin--creatinine ratio) provides additional kidney function information:
code: # With UACR risk_with_uacr <- ascvd_10y_prevent(   gender = "female",   age = 60,   sbp = 150,   bp_med = 1,   totchol = 220,   hdl = 55,   statin = 1,   diabetes = 1,   smoker = 0,   egfr = 75,   bmi = 32,   uacr = 150          # UACR in mg/g )

title: Using PREVENT Risk Score Functions
text: SDI captures socioeconomic factors using ZIP code:
code: # With ZIP code for SDI risk_with_sdi <- ascvd_10y_prevent(   gender = "male",   age = 52,   sbp = 135,   bp_med = 0,   totchol = 195,   hdl = 48,   statin = 0,   diabetes = 0,   smoker = 0,   egfr = 88,   bmi = 29,   zip = "02114"       # Boston, MA )

title: Using PREVENT Risk Score Functions
text: multiple optional predictors available:
code: # Full model with all optional predictors risk_full <- ascvd_10y_prevent(   gender = "female",   age = 58,   sbp = 145,   bp_med = 1,   totchol = 210,   hdl = 52,   statin = 1,   diabetes = 1,   smoker = 0,   egfr = 80,   bmi = 31,   hba1c = 7.2,   uacr = 100,   zip = "10001",   model = "auto"      # Will use full model )

title: Using PREVENT Risk Score Functions
text: can explicitly specify model use instead “auto”:
code: # Force base model even with optional predictors available risk_base_only <- ascvd_10y_prevent(   gender = "male",   age = 55,   sbp = 140,   bp_med = 0,   totchol = 213,   hdl = 50,   statin = 0,   diabetes = 1,   smoker = 0,   egfr = 90,   bmi = 30,   hba1c = 7.5,        # Available but will be ignored   model = "base"      # Explicitly use base model )

title: Using PREVENT Risk Score Functions
text: can specify PREVENT model variant using compute_CVrisk():
code: # Force base model for all PREVENT calculations results_base <- compute_CVrisk(   patient_data,   scores = c("ascvd_10y_prevent", "ascvd_30y_prevent"),   age = "age",   gender = "gender",   sbp = "sbp",   bp_med = "bp_med",   totchol = "totchol",   hdl = "hdl",   statin = "statin",   diabetes = "diabetes",   smoker = "smoker",   egfr = "egfr",   bmi = "bmi",   model = "base"      # Pass model parameter )

title: Using PREVENT Risk Score Functions
text: PREVENT functions return NA patients missing required predictors:
code: # Patient with missing eGFR risk_missing <- ascvd_10y_prevent(   gender = "male",   age = 55,   sbp = 140,   bp_med = 0,   totchol = 213,   hdl = 50,   statin = 0,   diabetes = 0,   smoker = 0,   egfr = NA,          # Missing   bmi = 30 )  print(risk_missing)   # Returns NA

title: Using PREVENT Risk Score Functions
text: PREVENT functions vectorized work efficiently data frames:
code: # Calculate risks for multiple patients at once ages <- c(45, 50, 55, 60) genders <- c("male", "female", "male", "female") sbps <- c(130, 140, 150, 160)  risks <- ascvd_10y_prevent(   gender = genders,   age = ages,   sbp = sbps,   bp_med = c(0, 0, 1, 1),   totchol = c(200, 210, 220, 230),   hdl = c(50, 45, 55, 48),   statin = c(0, 0, 0, 1),   diabetes = c(0, 0, 1, 1),   smoker = c(0, 1, 0, 0),   egfr = c(95, 90, 85, 80),   bmi = c(28, 30, 32, 34) )  print(risks)  # Returns vector of risks

title: Using PREVENT Risk Score Functions
text: PREVENT equations typically provide accurate risk estimates : Include kidney function (eGFR) standard predictor Include BMI instead just lipid levels Use recent data (updated cohorts) Better calibration contemporary populations Support 30-year risk estimation younger patients

what: Key Differences from ACC/AHA, Framingham, and MESA
title: Using PREVENT Risk Score Functions
text: table compares clinical parameters across available risk scores CVrisk: Key advantages PREVENT: - comprehensive risk factor assessment (includes kidney function via eGFR) - require race (reduces potential bias) - Accounts statin therapy - Offers optional predictors enhanced accuracy (HbA1c, UACR, socioeconomic factors) - Provides 10-year 30-year risk estimates
